hb.tipps: Saving tips for your biggest items
hb.tipp.miete: Check whether you can get housing benefit (Wohngeld). Have the service charge statement checked, for example by a tenants' association or with “Check a letter”.
hb.tipp.energie: Compare your electricity use with the Stromspiegel. Check your tariff and switching supplier. The energy advice of the consumer advice centre helps.
hb.tipp.handy: After the minimum term you can cancel mobile and internet contracts with one month's notice (§ 56 TKG). Then compare cheaper tariffs.
hb.tipp.vers: Above all, personal liability insurance is important. Check whether you have insurance twice or do not need it, for example for a phone or glasses.
hb.tipp.mobil: Check cheap tickets, for example the Deutschlandticket, a social ticket from your town or a job ticket. Ask your transport association or your town.
hb.tipp.essen: Plan the week and write a shopping list. Use own brands and special offers and use up leftovers. You find cheap recipes under “Save money”.
hb.tipp.kinder: For school supplies, lunch, trips and clubs there may be money from the education package (Bildung und Teilhabe). Also check the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag).
hb.tipp.raten: Do not take out a new loan to pay old debts. Non-profit debt advice is usually free, for example at welfare organisations, consumer advice centres or your town.
hb.tipp.sonst: Go through your subscriptions and memberships, for example streaming, gym or magazines. Cancel what you do not use.
hb.quelle.miete: Verbraucherzentrale (consumer advice centre); Deutscher Mieterbund; Housing Benefit Act (Wohngeld)
hb.quelle.mobil: Verbraucherzentrale; transport association in your region
hb.quelle.kinder: Education and participation package for children (§ 28 SGB II, § 34 SGB XII, § 6b BKGG); Familienkasse
hb.rb.h: Comparison with the standard rate (for orientation)
hb.rb.t: This much is planned in the standard rate (Regelbedarf) for a single adult ({b} per month). It is not a rule for you, only an orientation.
hb.rb.energie: Electricity and home upkeep (without rent and heating)
hb.rb.quelle: Source: Regelbedarfs-Ermittlungsgesetz (shares of consumer spending by category, § 5), standard rate level 1 for 2026; retrieved on 20.11.2026.
hb.hw.wb: {l}: the approval period ends on {d}. Apply for continued payment in good time.
hb.hw.wb.d: Without a new application, payment stops at the end of the approval period. Housing benefit (Wohngeld) is only paid from the month of the application. You apply to the office that pays the benefit.
hb.hw.ek: Your income has changed: before about {alt}, now about {neu}.
hb.hw.ek.d: If your income changes, an entitlement can change too. With Grundsicherungsgeld or social assistance (Sozialhilfe) you must report changes immediately (§ 60 Abs. 1 SGB I). With housing benefit (Wohngeld) you must report if your income rises permanently by more than 15 % (§ 27 Abs. 3 WoGG). With the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag) the change usually only counts at the next application. If in doubt, ask.
hb.hw.melden: Report the change to the office
hb.hw.briefLabel: Template for the notice (in German, you can change it)
hb.hw.knapp: Little is left. Check whether you are entitled to benefits.
hb.hw.knapp.d: Housing benefit (Wohngeld), child supplement (Kinderzuschlag) or Grundsicherungsgeld are possible even if you work. The benefits check shows what may apply to you.
hb.hw.nk: A back payment for service charges may be covered by the Jobcenter or social welfare office (Sozialamt).
hb.hw.nk.d: The back payment counts as housing costs in the month it is due (§ 22 Abs. 1 SGB II, § 35 SGB XII). This can help even if you do not otherwise receive benefits. Hand in the statement straight away. With “Check a letter” you can check the statement. Apply in the same month in which it is due.
hb.hw.kaputt: Something important is broken? A loan from the office may be possible.
hb.hw.kaputt.d: With Grundsicherungsgeld, the Jobcenter may give a loan for an essential need that cannot wait, for example a new fridge (§ 24 Abs. 1 SGB II). It is later deducted in instalments from the benefit (§ 42a SGB II). The social welfare office (Sozialamt) works similarly (§ 37 Abs. 1 SGB XII). Apply before you buy.
hb.hw.but: There may be money for school supplies, class trips, lunch or clubs.
hb.hw.but.d: Families with Grundsicherungsgeld, social assistance, housing benefit (Wohngeld) or child supplement (Kinderzuschlag) get the education package (Bildung und Teilhabe) (§ 28 SGB II, § 34 SGB XII, § 6b BKGG). The benefits check shows whether it may apply to you.
hb.hw.schulden: You pay instalments or debts. There is free help and the garnishment calculator.
hb.hw.schulden.d: Non-profit debt advice is usually free. A garnishment protection account (P-Konto) protects your money up to a limit.
hb.hw.tarif: You may be able to get an exemption from the broadcasting fee. Also ask about social tariffs.
hb.hw.tarif.d: With Grundsicherungsgeld, social assistance or basic income support in old age (Grundsicherung im Alter), an exemption from the broadcasting fee is possible (§ 4 Abs. 1 RBStV). You apply to the Beitragsservice. Ask your town about a social ticket and your provider about a social tariff.
hb.hw.tarif0: Ask about social tickets and social tariffs.
hb.hw.tarif0.d: Some towns have a social ticket for buses and trains, some providers a social tariff. Ask your town and your provider.
hb.wb.t: Enter the end date from your notice. Shortly before, the app reminds you when you open it.
hb.wb.sgb12: Basic income support in old age (Grundsicherung im Alter) (social welfare office (Sozialamt))
hb.wb.quelle: Usual periods: Grundsicherungsgeld usually 12 months (§ 41 Abs. 3 SGB II), basic income support in old age (Grundsicherung im Alter) usually 12 months (§ 44 Abs. 3 SGB XII), housing benefit (Wohngeld) usually 12 months (§ 25 Abs. 1 WoGG), child supplement (Kinderzuschlag) 6 months (§ 6a Abs. 7 BKGG). The date in your notice counts.
hb.hw.mb.schwanger: Are you pregnant? From the 13th week there is an additional need allowance (Mehrbedarf, more money each month) with Grundsicherungsgeld and social assistance (Sozialhilfe). Tell the office.
hb.hw.mb.schwanger.d: The additional need is {p} % of the standard rate (Regelbedarf) and applies until the end of the month of birth (§ 21 Abs. 2 SGB II, § 30 Abs. 2 SGB XII). In addition there is money for the initial equipment (baby things, maternity clothes), which you must apply for separately (§ 24 Abs. 3 SGB II). Show the Jobcenter or social welfare office (Sozialamt) your maternity record (Mutterpass) or a certificate.
hb.hw.mb.ww: Do you heat water with an electric water heater (Boiler) or instantaneous water heater (Durchlauferhitzer) in your flat? Then an additional need allowance (Mehrbedarf) is possible for it.
hb.hw.mb.ww.d: For adults it is {p} % of the standard rate (Regelbedarf), for children less (§ 21 Abs. 7 SGB II, § 30 Abs. 7 SGB XII). This only applies if the office does not already pay for hot water with the heating costs. Tell the office how hot water is produced in your flat. Higher costs only count with a separate meter.
hb.hw.mb.ern: Do you need special food because of an illness? Then more money is possible.
hb.hw.mb.ern.d: The law does not name a fixed amount (§ 21 Abs. 5 SGB II, § 30 Abs. 5 SGB XII). Offices usually follow the recommendations of the Deutscher Verein; not every diet counts. You need a certificate from a doctor.
hb.hw.mb.ae: Are you raising children under 18 on your own? There is an additional need allowance (Mehrbedarf) for this. Check whether it is included in your decision letter (Bescheid).
hb.hw.mb.ae.d: The amount depends on the number and age of the children, at most {max} % of the standard rate (Regelbedarf) (§ 21 Abs. 3 SGB II, § 30 Abs. 3 SGB XII). You are entitled to it if you care for the children alone. If it is missing from the decision: object (Widerspruch) within one month after you received the decision (§ 84 SGG).
hb.hw.mb.beh: With a disability there is an additional need allowance (Mehrbedarf) in certain cases, e.g. with help for work or training or with the mark G (Merkzeichen G).
hb.hw.mb.beh.d: With Grundsicherungsgeld: {p} % with benefits for participation in working life (§ 21 Abs. 4 SGB II). With social assistance (Sozialhilfe) also with mark G from pension age or with full reduction in earning capacity (volle Erwerbsminderung) (§ 30 Abs. 1 SGB XII). The benefits check already includes this if you enter it there.
hb.hw.mb.dauer: Do you have costs every month that you cannot avoid and that are much higher than usual? Then an additional need allowance (Mehrbedarf) is possible.
hb.hw.mb.dauer.d: Examples from practice: trips to see your child (contact rights), care and hygiene products for certain illnesses. The office checks each case individually; only “unavoidable” costs count (§ 21 Abs. 6 SGB II). With social assistance (Sozialhilfe) this is called a “higher standard rate” (§ 27a Abs. 4 SGB XII). Write down the costs and keep the receipts.
hb.hw.verm: Your savings ({b}) are close to the limit for {l} ({g}).
hb.hw.verm.bald: If about {r} is left over each month, you will reach the limit for {l} ({g}) in about {n} months.
hb.hw.verm.gg: Your savings ({b}) may be close to the limit for {l} (about {g}).
hb.hw.verm.gg.bald: If about {r} is left over each month, you may reach the limit for {l} (about {g}) in about {n} months.
hb.hw.verm.gg0: Your savings ({b}) may be close to the limit for {l}. How high it is depends on the age of each person.
hb.hw.verm.gg0.bald: If about {r} is left over each month, you may soon reach the limit for {l}. How high it is depends on the age of each person.
hb.hw.verm.wg: Your savings ({b}) are close to the guideline value (Richtwert) for {l} ({g}).
hb.hw.verm.wg.bald: If about {r} is left over each month, you will reach the guideline value (Richtwert) for {l} ({g}) in about {n} months.
hb.hw.verm.d.ggeld: With Grundsicherungsgeld, savings above the allowance count. Since 1.7.2026 it depends on age: under 30 {a}, from 30 {b}, from 40 {c}, from 50 {d} per person (§ 12 Abs. 2 SGB II). If your approval period (Bewilligungszeitraum) began before 1.7.2026, the old rules with other amounts still apply until it ends (§ 65a SGB II). A house or flat of usual size that you live in yourself does not count.
hb.hw.verm.d.gsa: With social assistance (Sozialhilfe, e.g. Grundsicherung im Alter), {a} per adult remain exempt, plus {k} for each person who is mainly supported (§ 90 Abs. 2 Nr. 9 SGB XII).
hb.hw.verm.d.wohngeld: The housing benefit (Wohngeld) act names no amount, only “substantial assets” (§ 21 Nr. 3 WoGG). Housing benefit offices (Wohngeldstelle) usually use {g1} for the first and {g2} for each further person (Nr. 21.37 WoGVwV). This is a guideline, not a fixed limit: it depends on the individual case.
hb.hw.verm.d.kiz: With the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag), {a} for the applicant and {b} for each further person remain exempt (§ 6a Abs. 3 BKGG). If the amount above it is less than your monthly Kinderzuschlag, only the first month is reduced.
hb.hw.verm.d2: This is only a guide. The office checks exactly what counts (account, car, pension savings). Do not spend or give away savings just to get a benefit: the office can then cut payments or demand money back (§ 34 SGB II, § 26 SGB XII). The “savings” figure comes from the benefits check.
hb.hw.pflege: You have marked care receipts totalling {b}. Submit them to the long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse). Then you may get money back.
hb.hw.pflege.d: The relief amount (Entlastungsbetrag, {e} per month, from care level (Pflegegrad) 1) is only reimbursed by the Pflegekasse against receipts, e.g. for recognised everyday help, day care (Tagespflege) or short-term care (Kurzzeitpflege) (§ 45b SGB XI). What you do not use in a year you can still use until 30.6. of the following year (§ 45b Abs. 1 SGB XI). Consumable care aids (e.g. gloves, bed protection) are paid by the fund up to {h} per month (§ 40 Abs. 2 SGB XI). For respite care (Verhinderungspflege) and short-term care (Kurzzeitpflege) there is, from care level 2, a combined amount of up to {j} per year (§ 42a SGB XI).
hb.hw.steuer: You may be able to claim some expenses in your tax return. Mark them with “Keep receipt”.
hb.hw.steuer.d: Household services, care and tradespeople: 20 % of the labour costs, at most {a} or {hw} tax reduction per year. Only with an invoice and bank transfer, not cash (§ 35a EStG). What the Pflegekasse or health insurance reimburses does not count. Medical costs (e.g. co-payments, glasses) count above a “reasonable burden” (§ 33 EStG). With a disability there is a lump sum; anyone who provides care unpaid gets a carer lump sum depending on the care level (Pflegegrad) (2: {p2}, 3: {p3}, 4 and 5: {p4}; § 33b EStG). Work equipment counts as income-related expenses; it pays off if everything together is more than {wk} per year (§ 9a EStG). If you have no or little taxable income, it usually brings nothing.
hb.beleg.vorschlag: Tip: For this expense it may be worth keeping the receipt.
hb.beleg.bar: Note: Tradesperson and household bills paid in cash do not count for tax (§ 35a EStG).
hb.bl.hinweis: The list does not replace the receipts. Keep the originals (paper or photo). The file is not protected. Only pass it on if you want to.
hb.en.knopf: Check your monthly instalment: Will you have to pay extra?
hb.en.lead: This takes about 3 minutes. You need your last bill or your electricity meter.
hb.en.heiz: How do you heat your home?
hb.en.heiz.miete: Through the rent (the landlord bills it)
hb.en.heiz.gas: With my own gas contract (gas boiler in the flat)
hb.en.heiz.andere: Other (oil, wood, coal, district heating with my own contract)
hb.en.abschlag.t: It is on your last bill or your bank statement.
hb.en.anzahl: How many times a year do you pay the instalment?
hb.en.anzahl.11: 11 times (one month is free, then the annual bill comes)
hb.en.weg: How do you know your consumption?
hb.en.weg.zaehler: I read the meter (two meter readings)
hb.en.z1: Meter reading at the last reading (kWh)
hb.en.z1.t: It is on your last bill, usually with a date.
hb.en.z2.t: Only the numbers before the decimal point. If your meter has two registers (for example HT and NT), add both together.
hb.en.jahr: Consumption on your last bill (kWh per year)
hb.en.gas.einheit: My gas meter shows cubic metres (m³). The bill says how many kWh one m³ is (calorific value × correction factor).
hb.en.preis.t: The unit price and standing charge are on the bill or in your contract. Leave them empty and SoLo estimates with the official average price. That is only rough.
hb.en.gp.fehlt: The standing charge is missing. Without it the result is too low.
hb.en.ww: Hot water comes from an electric boiler or instantaneous water heater
hb.en.ww.t: This also applies in the benefits check (there for the additional need).
hb.en.verbrauch.rechnung: According to the bill: {kwh} kWh per year.
hb.en.ungenau: The period is short. The result is not exact; in winter you usually use more.
hb.en.f.zahl: This number does not fit. Please check your entry. Up to 4 decimal places are allowed.
hb.en.saison: With heating, consumption is much higher in winter than in summer. The result is only reliable with meter readings covering almost a whole year. Or use the consumption from your last bill.
hb.en.alt: Your new meter reading is more than a month old. Please read the meter again and enter the reading with today's date.
hb.en.schaetz: Only a rough estimate with the average price of {ct} cents per kWh (Federal Statistical Office, 1st half of 2026, including standing charge and taxes). Your price may be very different. Enter your price from the bill to make it more exact.
hb.en.f.rueck: Today's meter reading is lower than the old one. Was the meter replaced? Then use the consumption from the bill.
hb.en.f.kurz: There must be at least 14 days between the readings.
hb.en.f.datum: The date is not right. The old reading must be before the new one, and no date may be in the future.
hb.en.f.null: Both meter readings are the same. SoLo cannot project anything. Please check the numbers.
hb.en.lang: There are more than 2 years between the readings. Better use the consumption from your last bill.
hb.en.hinweis: This is an estimate. The real bill may be different, for example because of price changes.
hb.en.dv.zeile: For comparison: a household with {n} uses about {kwh} kWh of electricity per year on average.
hb.en.dv.quelle: Source: Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), electricity consumption of private households by household size, figures for 2021. All types of housing, including households that heat with electricity. So only for orientation.
hb.en.dv.link: Compare more precisely with similar households: www.stromspiegel.de (co2online, not an official figure).
hb.en.anp.t: Are you using much less than last year? Then the supplier must take this into account appropriately in the instalment if you show it credibly, for example with a current meter reading (§ 41b Abs. 3 EnWG, § 13 Abs. 1 StromGVV/GasGVV). You cannot demand a specific amount. If an extra payment is likely, you can ask the supplier to raise the instalment, or put the money aside yourself. Then there is no big bill at the end.
hb.en.anp.sgb: If you receive Grundsicherungsgeld or social assistance and heat with gas: send a new gas instalment to the Jobcenter or social welfare office (Sozialamt) right away. It is part of your heating costs (§ 60 Abs. 1 Satz 1 Nr. 2 SGB I).
hb.en.anp.brief: Write a letter to the supplier
hb.en.nz.strom.sgb: Household electricity is included in the standard rate. So you generally have to pay an extra payment yourself. First ask the supplier about instalments. If a cut-off is threatened and there is no other way, you can apply for a loan at the Jobcenter (§ 24 Abs. 1 SGB II; for older debts § 22 Abs. 8 SGB II), and also at the social welfare office (Sozialamt) (§ 37 Abs. 1, § 36 SGB XII). You must apply for the loan separately. It is later withheld from your benefit in small amounts.
hb.en.nz.heiz.sgb: An extra payment for heating costs (also gas for heating or electricity for heating) is part of the costs of housing and heating. It counts in the month in which it is due, as far as the heating costs are reasonable (§ 22 Abs. 1 SGB II, § 35 Abs. 1 und 5 SGB XII). The office decides case by case whether it covers everything. Hand in the bill right away.
hb.en.nz.heiz.ohne: Even without ongoing benefits, a high extra payment for heating can create a claim to Grundsicherungsgeld for the month in which it is due. Apply in the same month in which the bill is due. Later it cannot be backdated (§ 37 Abs. 2 SGB II).
hb.en.nz.ww: Hot water with electricity: with Grundsicherungsgeld or social assistance you get an additional need allowance for it (§ 21 Abs. 7 SGB II, § 30 Abs. 7 SGB XII). SoLo checks this in the benefits check.
hb.en.nz.rb: The standard rate includes about {p} % for electricity and home maintenance, around {b} per month for a single person. This is not a rule, only for orientation.
hb.en.sperre.s: An electricity or gas cut-off is threatened
hb.en.sperre.raten: Are you on the basic supply tariff (Grundversorgung) and has the supplier already threatened a cut-off? Then you can demand a repayment agreement. The supplier must offer it to you within a week, with interest-free monthly instalments, usually over 6 to 18 months, or 12 to 24 months if you owe more than 300 €. If you accept it before the cut-off (best in writing), the supply must not be cut off as long as you pay the instalments and the current monthly payments (§ 41g Abs. 1 EnWG). With other contracts: ask for instalments anyway.
hb.en.ssc: The Stromspar-Check by Caritas and energy agencies is free for households with a low income: advice at home or online, energy-saving devices such as LED lamps and water-saving shower heads, a grant for a new fridge. Appointments via stromspar-check.de or free of charge on 0800 4443322. Funded by the Federal Environment Ministry.
hb.en.wie: Consumption per day = (meter reading today − old meter reading) ÷ days in between; times 365 = annual consumption. Costs = annual consumption × unit price + 12 × standing charge. Instalments = instalment × number of instalments per year (12 or 11). If the difference is at most {tolEur} or at most {tolProz} % of the costs, it counts as “about right” (a rule of thumb by SoLo, not a legal limit). SoLo always calculates for a whole year. Your bill may cover a different period.
hb.en.frage.ww: The benefits check says something different about hot water. Do you want to change it there too?
hb.en.frage.plan: The plan shows {alt} for electricity and gas. Use {neu} instead?
hb.en.druck: Energy: extra payment possible, about {b} (estimated from own information).
hb.hw.energie: An extra payment for electricity or gas is possible. Check your instalment.
hb.hw.energie.d: From your information SoLo estimates an extra payment of about {b}. A higher instalment spreads the costs over the year.
